title: Gather a batch within a deadline

blocks.text: The page's batch execution: `invokeAll(tasks)` submits every task, waits until all are done and returns their `Future`s **in the same order as the input**. `invokeAll(tasks, timeout, unit)` also cancels the tasks that have not finished when the time runs out. The page's best practices recommend that timed form, so one slow task cannot hold up the whole batch.
Write `Gather.all(executor, tasks, timeout, unit, fallback)`, returning one result per task, in the order of `tasks`:

items: the task's result if it finished;
`fallback` if the task threw, or if it was still running at the deadline and so was cancelled.

blocks.text: The timeout is **one deadline for the whole batch**, counted from the call, not a fresh wait per task.

rows: three tasks where the last finishes first and the first finishes last
`[1, -1]`, and the unfinished task is cancelled, freeing its thread

cases.says: Every task's result is gathered once the whole batch is done.
Results follow the order of the tasks, not the order in which they finished.
A task that threw gives the fallback in its place, and the other results are kept.
A task still running at the deadline is cancelled and gives the fallback, since get() on it throws CancellationException.
The timeout is one deadline for the whole batch: a task that ends only after 300 ms in total gives the fallback, even if it took under 300 ms itself.

concepts: invokeAll() waits for every task and returns their Futures in the order of the input, whatever order they finished in.
invokeAll() with a timeout cancels the tasks that have not finished when the time runs out.
